title: Tinikling (bamboo pole hop)
summary: Tinikling is a dance of the Philippines in which two players kneel at the ends of two long bamboo poles and beat them on blocks and together in a three-beat bar while the dancer hops in and out between them, taking care not to be caught. It is named after the tikling, a bird that steps nimbly through grass.
howToPlay: The poles are beaten twice on the blocks (Tap, Tap) and then clapped together (Clap) on the third beat. The dancer hops In between the poles and Out in front of them.
A ring closes on a place when it is time. Tap Tap and Clap as the poles meet, and In and Out as the dancer's feet land.
Start with the basic three-beat step, then try the quick step.
rules: A tap right on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and taps with no ring open cost points.
Each pattern is played twice through, counted in threes.
Patterns are simplified teaching figures in the style of the dance, not a performance set.
heritageNote: Tinikling is among the best known folk dances of the Philippines and is taught in schools and danced at festivals at home and abroad. Players take turns on the poles, because holding them is as skilled as dancing.
